newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian debt firm, awaiting word from RBA.
newsitem.headline: Australian debt firm, awaiting word from RBA.

text.p: *Australian debt futures remained close to the highs seen in after hours trading as the market held onto the possibility of the RBA announcing an official rate cut.
*Policy changes usually announced at 9.30 a.m. (2330 GMT)

Australian debt futures remained close to the highs seen in after hours trading as the market held on to the possibility of the Reserve Bank announcing an official rate cut following Thursday's weak labour force data.
September bill futures touched a high 94.92, and all but pricing in a 50 basis point cut in official rates.

"Today is the Reserve Bank's first opportunity. Governor Macfarlane had discretion coming out of the early May board meeting. It is possible he has discretion coming out of the early June meeting," said Rory Robertson, fixed interest strategist at Bankers Trust Australia.
The RBA last cut official interest rates to 5.5 percent on May 23, over two weeks after the May board meeting.
"Who knows, he (Macfarlane) may have an easing in his in tray, but you can't say anything with confidence. The markets have it fully factored in," Robertson told Reuters Financial Television (RFTV).
The market will be glued to their trading screens at 9.30 a.m. (2330 GMT) when the RBA usually announces policy changes.
Bond futures were also firm with the June 10-year contract close to December's 93.015 peak, which if broken would take the equivalent cash rate below 7.0 percent.
